questions.question: Memory hierarchy is the arrangement of different memory types according to:
questions.explanation: The memory hierarchy arranges memory types by speed, capacity and cost.

questions.question: Which is the fastest memory in the hierarchy?
questions.explanation: CPU registers sit inside the processor and are the fastest memory.

questions.question: Cache memory is commonly built using:
questions.explanation: Cache memory is built with SRAM, which is fast.

questions.question: Main memory is commonly built using:
questions.explanation: Main memory is commonly built with DRAM.

questions.question: The two types of locality of reference are:
questions.explanation: The two types of locality of reference are temporal and spatial.

questions.question: Temporal locality means that:

options.D: Recently accessed data is likely to be accessed again soon

questions.explanation: Temporal locality means recently accessed data is likely to be accessed again soon.

questions.question: Spatial locality means that:

options.A: Nearby memory locations are likely to be accessed soon

questions.explanation: Spatial locality means nearby memory locations are likely to be accessed soon.

questions.question: RAM is generally:
questions.explanation: RAM loses its contents when power is off, so it is volatile.

questions.question: SRAM stores each bit using:
questions.explanation: SRAM stores each bit using flip-flops.

questions.question: DRAM requires:
questions.explanation: DRAM stores bits in capacitors that leak charge, so it needs periodic refreshing.

questions.question: Compared with SRAM, DRAM is:
questions.explanation: DRAM is cheaper per bit than SRAM, though it is slower.

questions.question: Magnetic tape is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: Magnetic tape is mainly used for backup and archival storage.

questions.question: As we move down the memory hierarchy, capacity generally:
questions.explanation: Moving down the hierarchy, capacity generally increases.

questions.question: As we move down the memory hierarchy, cost per bit generally:
questions.explanation: Moving down the hierarchy, cost per bit generally decreases.

questions.question: Memory allocation means:

options.A: Assigning available main memory space to processes

questions.explanation: Memory allocation assigns available main memory space to processes.

questions.question: Memory allocation schemes are broadly classified into:
questions.explanation: Memory allocation schemes are classified as contiguous and non-contiguous.

questions.question: In contiguous allocation, a process occupies:

options.B: A single continuous block of memory

questions.explanation: In contiguous allocation a process occupies a single continuous block of memory.

questions.question: Examples of non-contiguous allocation are:
questions.explanation: Paging and segmentation are examples of non-contiguous allocation.

questions.question: Internal fragmentation is:

options.A: Unused space inside an allocated partition

questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation is unused space inside an allocated partition.

questions.question: External fragmentation occurs when:

options.C: Free memory is split into small non-contiguous holes

questions.explanation: External fragmentation occurs when free memory is split into small non-contiguous holes.

questions.question: Compaction is used to:

options.D: Combine scattered free holes into one large block

questions.explanation: Compaction combines scattered free holes into one large block.

questions.question: Fixed partitioning is also called:
questions.explanation: Fixed partitioning is also called static partitioning.

questions.question: Variable partitioning is also called:
questions.explanation: Variable partitioning is also called dynamic partitioning.

questions.question: The formula for internal fragmentation in a fixed partition is:
questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation equals partition size minus process size.

questions.question: Which fragmentation is common in fixed partitioning?
questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation is common in fixed partitioning.

questions.question: Which fragmentation is common in variable partitioning?
questions.explanation: External fragmentation is common in variable partitioning.

questions.question: First Fit allocates:

options.C: The first hole that is large enough

questions.explanation: First Fit allocates the first hole that is large enough.

questions.question: Best Fit allocates:

options.A: The smallest hole that is large enough

questions.explanation: Best Fit allocates the smallest hole that is large enough.

questions.question: Worst Fit allocates:
questions.explanation: Worst Fit allocates the largest available hole.

questions.question: Next Fit starts the search from:

options.B: The position of the previous allocation

questions.explanation: Next Fit starts searching from the position of the previous allocation.

questions.question: In paging, a process is divided into fixed-size blocks called:
questions.explanation: In paging, a process is divided into fixed-size blocks called pages.

questions.question: In paging, physical memory is divided into blocks called:
questions.explanation: In paging, physical memory is divided into blocks called frames.

questions.question: In basic paging, page size is:
questions.explanation: In basic paging, the page size equals the frame size.

questions.question: The data structure that maps pages to frames is the:
questions.explanation: The page table maps pages to frames.

questions.question: The MMU is responsible for:

options.A: Translating logical addresses into physical addresses

questions.explanation: The MMU translates logical addresses into physical addresses.

questions.question: The TLB is:

options.C: A small, fast memory that stores recently used page table entries

questions.explanation: The TLB is a small, fast memory that stores recently used page table entries.

questions.question: A TLB hit occurs when:

options.B: The page table entry is found in the TLB

questions.explanation: A TLB hit occurs when the page table entry is found in the TLB.

questions.question: Basic paging eliminates:
questions.explanation: Basic paging eliminates external fragmentation, although the last page may waste space.

questions.question: A logical address in paging consists of:
questions.explanation: A logical address in paging consists of a page number and an offset.

questions.question: Virtual memory allows a process to:

options.B: Run only when fully in RAM
options.C: Execute without its entire program being in RAM

questions.explanation: Virtual memory lets a process execute without its entire program being in RAM.

questions.question: A page fault occurs when:

options.A: The page is present in memory
options.B: The required page is not present in physical memory

questions.explanation: A page fault occurs when the required page is not present in physical memory.

questions.question: Page replacement means:

options.D: Removing an existing page to load another page

questions.explanation: Page replacement removes an existing page to load another page.

questions.question: FIFO replaces:
questions.explanation: FIFO replaces the page that was loaded earliest.

questions.question: A page hit means that the required page is:
questions.explanation: A page hit means the required page is already present in a frame.

questions.question: Belady's Anomaly is a situation where:

options.A: More frames always reduce page faults

questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly is when increasing the number of frames increases page faults.

questions.question: Which algorithm is known for Belady's Anomaly?
questions.explanation: FIFO is the algorithm known for Belady's Anomaly.

questions.question: The Logical Address Space is given by:
questions.explanation: The Logical Address Space is 2^LA bytes for an LA-bit address.

questions.question: The number of pages N is given by:
questions.explanation: The number of pages is the logical address space divided by the page size, N = LAS / PS.

questions.question: The number of offset bits d is given by:
questions.explanation: The number of offset bits is d = log2(PS).

questions.question: In a page table entry, the dirty bit indicates that the page:
questions.explanation: The dirty bit shows that the page has been modified.

questions.question: Memory hierarchy works effectively mainly because of:
questions.explanation: The hierarchy works well mainly because of locality of reference.

questions.question: Which is the correct order from fastest to slowest?
questions.explanation: From fastest to slowest the order is registers, cache, RAM, SSD/HDD, tape.

questions.question: Which statement about SRAM and DRAM is correct?

options.A: DRAM is faster and costlier than SRAM
options.D: SRAM is faster and costlier, and needs no refresh

questions.explanation: SRAM is faster and costlier than DRAM and needs no refresh.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT secondary storage?
questions.explanation: Main memory (RAM) is primary memory, not secondary storage.

questions.question: On a cache miss, the system generally:
questions.explanation: On a cache miss the system generally accesses RAM.

questions.question: Under virtual memory, when a required page is not in RAM, the system accesses:
questions.explanation: When a page is not in RAM, the system accesses secondary storage.

questions.question: Sequentially accessing array elements A[0], A[1], A[2] shows:
questions.explanation: Accessing A[0], A[1], A[2] in order shows spatial locality.

questions.question: The repeatedly used variable "sum" in a loop shows:
questions.explanation: Repeated use of the variable "sum" in a loop shows temporal locality.

questions.question: A process needs 80 KB but is given a 100 KB partition. The internal fragmentation is:
questions.explanation: Internal fragmentation is 100 KB - 80 KB = 20 KB.

questions.question: A process of 70 KB is placed in a 100 KB fixed partition. The wasted space is:
questions.explanation: The wasted space is 100 KB - 70 KB = 30 KB.

questions.question: Free holes of 10 KB, 20 KB and 30 KB exist, and a process needs 50 KB contiguous memory. What happens?

options.B: It cannot be allocated because of external fragmentation
options.C: It creates internal fragmentation of 10 KB

questions.explanation: The holes total 60 KB, but no single hole is 50 KB or more, so external fragmentation prevents allocation.

questions.question: A limitation of compaction is that:

options.D: Moving processes takes time and may need address relocation

questions.explanation: Compaction takes time because processes must be moved, and addresses may need relocation.

questions.question: An advantage of unequal-sized fixed partitions over equal-sized ones is that they:

options.A: Can accommodate different process sizes more suitably

questions.explanation: Unequal-sized partitions can fit different process sizes more suitably.

questions.question: In fixed partitioning, the maximum number of resident processes is limited by:
questions.explanation: The number of resident processes is limited by the number of partitions.

questions.question: A process larger than the largest fixed partition:
questions.explanation: A process larger than the largest fixed partition cannot be loaded.

questions.question: In variable partitioning, a partition is:

options.D: Created dynamically according to the process's requirement

questions.explanation: In variable partitioning a partition is created dynamically for the process's requirement.

questions.question: Free holes are 100 KB, 500 KB, 200 KB and 300 KB. A process of 180 KB arrives. Best Fit selects:
questions.explanation: Best Fit picks the smallest hole that is at least 180 KB, which is 200 KB.

questions.question: In the same case (holes 100, 500, 200, 300 KB; process 180 KB), First Fit selects:
questions.explanation: First Fit picks the first hole big enough; 100 KB is too small, so the 500 KB hole is chosen.

questions.question: In the same case, Worst Fit selects:
questions.explanation: Worst Fit picks the largest hole, 500 KB.

questions.question: Why can a process fail to load although the total free memory is large enough?

options.D: No single contiguous hole may be large enough

questions.explanation: A process can fail to load because no single contiguous hole may be large enough.

questions.question: In non-contiguous allocation using paging, the pages of a process are:
questions.explanation: With paging, the pages of a process can be stored in any available frames.

questions.question: A logical address of 4 bits gives a Logical Address Space of:
questions.explanation: A 4-bit address gives 2^4 = 16 bytes.

questions.question: A physical address of 5 bits gives a Physical Address Space of:
questions.explanation: A 5-bit address gives 2^5 = 32 bytes.

questions.question: LAS = 64 KB and PS = 4 KB. The number of pages is:
questions.explanation: The number of pages is 64 KB / 4 KB = 16.

questions.question: For 16 pages, the number of page-number bits is:
questions.explanation: 16 pages need log2(16) = 4 bits.

questions.question: PAS = 64 KB and FS = 4 KB. The number of frames is:
questions.explanation: The number of frames is 64 KB / 4 KB = 16.

questions.question: A page size of 4 KB needs how many offset bits?
questions.explanation: A 4 KB page is 2^12 bytes, so 12 offset bits are needed.

questions.question: A logical address has 16 bits and the offset is 10 bits. The number of page-number bits is:
questions.explanation: The page-number bits are 16 - 10 = 6.

questions.question: A physical address has 15 bits and the offset is 10 bits. The number of frame-number bits is:
questions.explanation: The frame-number bits are 15 - 10 = 5.

questions.question: A page table has 16 entries and each entry is 4 bytes. The page table size is:
questions.explanation: The page table size is 16 x 4 = 64 bytes.

questions.question: A page table has 32 entries of 16 bits each. The size in bytes is:
questions.explanation: 32 entries x 2 bytes (16 bits) = 64 bytes.

questions.question: For logical address 20 and page size 8 bytes, the page number and offset are:
questions.explanation: 20 = 2 x 8 + 4, so the page number is 2 and the offset is 4.

questions.question: Page 2 is in Frame 5, frame size is 8 bytes and the offset is 4. The physical address is:
questions.explanation: Physical address = 5 x 8 + 4 = 44.

questions.question: A process of 10 KB with 4 KB pages has internal fragmentation of:
questions.explanation: 10 KB needs 3 pages of 4 KB (12 KB), so 2 KB is wasted.

questions.question: The maximum internal fragmentation of one process in paging is:
questions.explanation: The last page can waste at most less than one page size.

questions.question: A TLB miss:

options.A: Does not necessarily cause a page fault

questions.explanation: A TLB miss only means the entry is not in the TLB; the page may still be in memory.

questions.question: In the EMAT model, the access time on a TLB hit is:
questions.explanation: On a TLB hit the time is T + M.

questions.question: In the EMAT model, the access time on a TLB miss is:
questions.explanation: On a TLB miss the time is T + 2M, with an extra access to the page table.

questions.question: T = 10 ns, M = 100 ns and H = 0.8. The EMAT is:
T = 5 ns, M = 80 ns and H = 0.9. The EMAT is:
T = 10 ns, M = 100 ns and EMAT = 120 ns. The hit ratio is:
T = 5 ns, M = 50 ns and H = 0.7. The EMAT is:
System A (T = 10, M = 100, H = 80%) and System B (T = 5, M = 100, H = 90%). Which is faster?
questions.explanation: System A has EMAT 130 ns and System B has 115 ns, so B is faster.

questions.question: The virtual address space can be:

options.A: Only smaller than the physical address space
options.B: Only equal to the physical address space
options.C: Only larger than the physical address space
options.D: Smaller than, equal to or larger than the physical address space

questions.explanation: The virtual address space can be smaller than, equal to or larger than the physical address space.

questions.question: For 3 frames and the reference string 1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, FIFO gives how many page faults?
questions.explanation: With 3 frames FIFO gives faults on 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 1, 2, 3, which is 8 faults.

questions.question: For the same string with 3 frames, how many page hits occur under FIFO?
questions.explanation: The two hits are the second reference to 1 and the second reference to 2.

questions.question: The page fault ratio for that example (8 faults in 10 references) is:
questions.explanation: The page fault ratio is 8 / 10 = 0.8.

questions.question: In the Belady's anomaly example string, FIFO gives:
questions.explanation: For the standard Belady string, FIFO gives 9 faults with 3 frames and 10 faults with 4 frames.

questions.question: In a string with 12 references, 9 faults and 3 hits, the hit ratio is:
questions.explanation: The hit ratio is 3 / 12 = 25%.

questions.question: Three frames contain pages 4, 5, 6, loaded in that order. FIFO replaces:
questions.explanation: FIFO replaces the oldest loaded page, which is 4.

questions.question: Which statement about moving UP the memory hierarchy is correct?

options.A: Capacity increases and cost per bit decreases
options.B: Capacity decreases, access time decreases and cost per bit increases
options.C: Capacity increases and access time decreases
options.D: Speed decreases and cost per bit increases

questions.explanation: Moving up the hierarchy, capacity decreases, access time decreases and cost per bit increases.

questions.question: Which pairing is WRONG?
questions.explanation: Registers have the smallest capacity, not the largest.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares variable and fixed partitioning?

options.A: Variable partitioning creates partitions per process, reducing internal fragmentation but allowing external fragmentation
options.B: Variable partitioning has fixed partitions and internal fragmentation

questions.explanation: Variable partitioning creates partitions per process, reducing internal fragmentation but allowing external fragmentation.

questions.question: Free memory is 120 KB in gaps of 40 KB, 30 KB and 50 KB. A process needs 90 KB contiguous memory. What happens?

options.A: It is allocated in the 50 KB gap
options.B: It is allocated after compaction automatically
options.C: Allocation fails because of external fragmentation
options.D: It is allocated using internal fragmentation

questions.explanation: The largest gap is 50 KB, which is less than the 90 KB needed, so allocation fails.

questions.question: There is 200 KB of free memory in separate holes. Whether a 150 KB contiguous request succeeds depends on:

options.B: The size of the largest hole

questions.explanation: A contiguous request succeeds only if the largest single hole is big enough.

questions.question: Which statement about non-contiguous allocation is FALSE?

options.A: The pages of a process must occupy consecutive frames
options.B: Pages can be placed in different frames
options.C: A mapping structure is used for translation

questions.explanation: The statement is false because pages need not occupy consecutive frames.

questions.question: Fixed partitions are 100 KB, 200 KB and 300 KB, all free. A 280 KB process arrives. It goes to the:
questions.explanation: Only the 300 KB partition can hold a 280 KB process.

questions.question: Fixed partitions are 100 KB, 200 KB and 300 KB; the 100 KB and 300 KB partitions are free. A 150 KB process arrives. What happens?

options.A: It uses both free partitions together
options.B: It goes to the 100 KB partition
options.C: It goes to the 300 KB partition

questions.explanation: The 200 KB partition is occupied, so the 150 KB process goes to the free 300 KB partition.

questions.question: A system has four fixed partitions, all occupied, and six processes arrive. How many can reside in the partitions at once?
questions.explanation: Only four processes can reside at a time, one per partition.

questions.question: A 400 KB free hole is split to allocate a 120 KB process. The remaining 280 KB:

options.D: Is given to the next process automatically

questions.explanation: The remaining 280 KB becomes a new free hole.

questions.question: Holes are 80 KB, 160 KB and 240 KB, and a 150 KB process arrives. Which strategy chooses the 160 KB hole?
questions.explanation: Best Fit chooses the smallest hole that is large enough, the 160 KB hole.

questions.question: For the same holes (80, 160, 240 KB) and a 150 KB process, Worst Fit selects:
questions.explanation: Worst Fit chooses the largest hole, 240 KB.

questions.question: Which statement about compaction is INCORRECT?

options.A: It increases the total amount of free memory

questions.explanation: Compaction does not increase total free memory; it only gathers it into one block.

questions.question: Before compaction: P1 (100 KB), Free 20 KB, P2 (150 KB), Free 30 KB, P3 (100 KB), Free 50 KB. After compaction the combined free space is:
questions.explanation: After compaction the free space is 20 + 30 + 50 = 100 KB.

questions.question: If LAS = 32 KB and PS = 2 KB, the number of pages is:
questions.explanation: The number of pages is 32 KB / 2 KB = 16.

questions.question: A system has a 20-bit logical address and a 4 KB page size. The number of pages is:
questions.explanation: With a 4 KB page (12 offset bits), a 20-bit address has 8 page bits, so 2^8 = 256 pages.

questions.question: For a page size of 8 KB in a byte-addressable system, the number of offset bits is:
questions.explanation: An 8 KB page is 2^13 bytes, so 13 offset bits are needed.

questions.question: Physical memory has 128 frames. The frame number needs:
questions.explanation: 128 frames need log2(128) = 7 bits.

questions.question: A page table has 256 entries of 4 bytes each. Its size is:
questions.explanation: 256 x 4 bytes = 1024 bytes = 1 KB.

questions.question: For logical address 29 and page size 8 bytes, the page number and offset are:
questions.explanation: 29 = 3 x 8 + 5, so the page number is 3 and the offset is 5.

questions.question: Page 3 maps to Frame 6, the frame size is 16 bytes and the offset is 4. The physical address is:
questions.explanation: Physical address = 6 x 16 + 4 = 100.

questions.question: LA = 16 bits, PS = 1 KB and PTE = 2 bytes. The page table size is:
questions.explanation: There are 2^(16-10) = 64 pages, so the table size is 64 x 2 = 128 bytes.

questions.question: LA = 32 bits, PS = 4 KB and PTE = 4 bytes. The single-level page table size is:
questions.explanation: There are 2^20 pages, so the table size is 2^20 x 4 bytes = 4 MB.

questions.question: A process of 17 KB with a 4 KB page size has internal fragmentation of:
questions.explanation: 17 KB needs 5 pages of 4 KB (20 KB), so 3 KB is wasted.

questions.question: A page is present in RAM but its translation is not in the TLB. This is a:
questions.explanation: If the page is in RAM but its entry is not in the TLB, it is a TLB miss, not a page fault.

questions.question: If the TLB hit ratio is 100% and the TLB access time is negligible, EMAT is approximately:
questions.explanation: With a 100% hit ratio and negligible T, EMAT is about T + M, approximately M.

questions.question: T = 20 ns, M = 100 ns and H = 0.75. The EMAT is:
With T = 10 ns and M = 100 ns, what hit ratio gives EMAT = 130 ns?
If the hit ratio increases while T and M stay constant, EMAT:
questions.explanation: A higher hit ratio means fewer slow miss accesses, so EMAT decreases.

questions.question: The TLB miss time is greater than the hit time because:

options.A: An extra page table access in memory is needed

questions.explanation: A TLB miss needs an extra memory access to read the page table.

questions.question: For 3 frames and reference string 7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4, FIFO gives how many page faults?
questions.explanation: FIFO with 3 frames faults on 7, 0, 1, 2, 3, 0 and 4, which is 7 faults.

questions.question: For the same string (7, 0, 1, 2, 0, 3, 0, 4) with 3 frames, the number of FIFO hits is:
questions.explanation: The only hit is the second reference to page 0, so there is 1 hit.

questions.question: A FIFO queue holds pages 2, 7, 4 (2 entered first). A hit occurs on page 7. The next replacement is:
questions.explanation: FIFO ignores hits, so the oldest page, 2, is replaced next.

questions.question: With 4 frames loaded with pages 1, 2, 3, 4 in order, page 5 arrives. FIFO replaces:
questions.explanation: FIFO replaces the oldest loaded page, which is 1.

questions.question: If there are 50 references and the hit ratio is 60%, the number of page faults is:
questions.explanation: With a 60% hit ratio, 40% of 50 references are faults, which is 20.

questions.question: If 80 references give 64 hits, the page fault percentage is:
questions.explanation: The faults are 80 - 64 = 16, which is 20% of 80.

questions.question: Which property distinguishes FIFO from LRU?

options.A: FIFO uses frequency; LRU uses page size
options.B: FIFO uses arrival time; LRU uses recent usage
options.C: Both always replace the same page

questions.explanation: FIFO uses arrival time, while LRU uses recent usage.

questions.question: Which statement about Belady's Anomaly is correct?

options.A: It is associated with FIFO but does not occur for every reference string
options.D: It means fewer frames always cause fewer faults

questions.explanation: Belady's Anomaly is associated with FIFO but does not occur for every reference string.

questions.question: In the FIFO pseudocode, on a page fault the algorithm:

options.C: Replaces the page at the FIFO pointer and moves the pointer to the next frame

questions.explanation: On a fault, FIFO replaces the page at the FIFO pointer and moves the pointer to the next frame.

questions.question: A disadvantage of FIFO is that it:

options.D: May remove a frequently used page

questions.explanation: A disadvantage of FIFO is that it may remove a frequently used page.

questions.question: Which items are stored in a page table entry (PTE)?

options.A: Frame number, valid bit, protection bits, reference bit and dirty bit

questions.explanation: A PTE holds the frame number plus valid, protection, reference and dirty bits.

questions.question: The dirty bit is used to know whether:

options.D: The page is in the TLB

questions.explanation: The dirty bit shows whether the page has been modified.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares paging and segmentation?

options.D: Paging uses fixed-size pages; segmentation uses variable-size segments

questions.explanation: Paging uses fixed-size pages, whereas segmentation uses variable-size segments.

questions.question: Which fragmentation pairing is correct?
questions.explanation: Paging has internal fragmentation (in the last page), while segmentation has external fragmentation.

questions.question: A key advantage of virtual memory is that:

options.A: Programs larger than the available RAM can execute

questions.explanation: Virtual memory lets programs larger than the available RAM execute.

questions.question: A disadvantage of virtual memory is that:

options.B: Accessing pages from secondary storage is much slower than RAM and page tables use extra memory

questions.explanation: Accessing pages from secondary storage is much slower than RAM, and page tables use extra memory.

questions.question: A system records 720 TLB hits out of 900 memory references. The hit ratio is:
questions.explanation: The hit ratio is 720 / 900 = 0.8.

questions.question: A system has 8 GB RAM and a process with a 16 GB virtual address space. Which is true?

options.B: The process must occupy 16 GB RAM
options.D: The virtual address space can be larger than physical RAM

questions.explanation: A virtual address space can be larger than physical RAM, so the process can run.

questions.question: Which is NOT an objective of memory allocation?
questions.explanation: Increasing page faults is not an objective of memory allocation.

questions.question: Memory allocation supports multiprogramming by:

options.A: Letting multiple processes reside in RAM at the same time
options.B: Allowing only one process in RAM
options.D: Running only after a process ends

questions.explanation: Memory allocation supports multiprogramming by letting multiple processes reside in RAM at the same time.
